extracted.intended_audience: Wattpad writers and readers (authors trying to understand/optimize rankings)
extracted.subtask_description: Explains the factors believed to govern Wattpad's YuenRank hashtag/genre rankings and what authors can do (or avoid) to influence visibility. Focuses on engagement, recency, read behavior, and platform-specific quirks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent New Daily Reads
rubrics_metrics.description: How many new reads the book gets each day versus how many it usually gets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article lists this as a suspected factor; spikes in daily reads matter more for smaller books because the algorithm evaluates books relative to their usual patterns (e.g., 500 extra readers is a much larger percentage increase for a 1k-read book than for a 1m-read book).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vote-to-Read Ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: How many votes a book receives for each new read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ratio of explicit positive feedback (votes) to raw reads is suspected to influence rankings—higher engagement per read likely signals stronger community approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment-to-Read Ratio
rubrics_metrics.description: How many comments a book receives for each new read.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments per read indicate active engagement; higher comment rates per reader are likely weighted positively by the ranking system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Times Added to Reading Lists
rubrics_metrics.description: How often readers add the book to public reading lists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Being added to reading lists is an explicit signal of interest/curation and is suspected to contribute to a book's popularity ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of Times Added to Private Libraries
rubrics_metrics.description: How often readers add the book to their private libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private-library adds indicate personal bookmarks/interest and are listed as a separate engagement metric that may affect rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average Consecutive Read Time
rubrics_metrics.description: The length of uninterrupted time the average reader spends reading a book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer consecutive read times suggest sustained engagement; the article lists this as a suspected behavioral metric that likely improves ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentage of Completed Reads
rubrics_metrics.description: The percentage of readers who finish the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion rate is a quality/engagement signal—higher percentages of readers finishing the story are likely to boost ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recent Updates (Recency)
rubrics_metrics.description: How recently the story has been changed or edited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recency of updates is apparently prioritized by the system; recently-updated stories are favored in rankings, which can disadvantage completed works that are no longer updated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique Readers
rubrics_metrics.description: The number of separate people reading the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unique reader counts (as distinct from raw reads which may include repeats) are likely tracked and used to determine popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative Growth Compared to Historical Baseline
rubrics_metrics.description: Books are evaluated in the context of their own previous patterns—percent changes matter more than absolute counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A given spike in readers affects a small book much more (percentage-wise) than a very large one; the algorithm likely normalizes for a book's historical baseline to give smaller stories a fair shot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reads-per-Chapter (chapter-normalized reads)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average reads divided by number of chapters (reads-per-chapter) as a normalization metric.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article speculates the system may use reads-per-chapter; adding chapters can lower this average (e.g., 10k reads across 10 chapters = 1k/read-per-chapter; adding a chapter reduces that average), which can unintentionally penalize authors who add chapters to older works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Completed Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Completed books appear to be disadvantaged because they are not being updated and the system favors recent updates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page identifies this as a flaw: rankings 'fail to promote completed stories' and prioritize recently-updated content, causing user frustration and discouraging finishing stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative Effect of New Chapters on Abandoned/Old Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding a chapter to an abandoned or long-unupdated story can decrease certain normalized metrics and hurt ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically, adding chapters can reduce reads-per-chapter and thus lower a story's standing; this counterintuitive effect means authors may be discouraged from finishing older works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community Social Activity Model (votes/comments/shares)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ranking was modeled after community-driven systems like Digg and Reddit that rely on social activity to determine popularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Yuen (creator) designed the algorithm to reflect community engagement; the article uses this to explain why votes, comments, and other social signals matter to ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested Quality Variable (writing quality/error rate)
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed metric to incorporate quality—e.g., measures of writing quality or error/rate of poor writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article recommends Wattpad implement a 'quality variable' to help weed out poorly-written or error-ridden content; this is presented as a desired addition rather than a currently confirmed factor.
